title: What If the Sahara Turned Green Again?

scenes.text: What if the Sahara turned green again? It already has, and not that long ago.
From about 11,000 to 5,000 years ago, roughly nine million square kilometers of North Africa were green.
Lakes filled old basins. Hippos, elephants and giraffes lived there, and ancient cave paintings show them.
The cause was a wobble in Earth's orbit. It gave the north about 7 percent more summer sunlight and strengthened the African monsoon.
Then it ended fast, in about 200 years. Today the Sahara blows about five times more dust than it did then.
Will it return? The next summer sunlight peak is about 10,000 years away. Don't pack for hippos yet.

description:
What if the Sahara turned green again?
It was green until about 5,000 years ago, thanks to a wobble in Earth's orbit.
